experiment: YOLOv8n object detection on COCO128 split

dataset.name: COCO128 (ultralytics official demo set)
dataset.note: Official coco128.yaml leaks train into val; a disjoint split was carved with seed 42.

conclusions: Zero-shot pretrained YOLOv8n achieves mAP50 0.636 on the held-out 28-image test set without any COCO128 training.
Fine-tuning at lr=1e-3 gives mAP50 0.630 (mAP50-95 0.455), essentially unchanged from zero-shot.
Fine-tuning at default lr=1e-2 gives mAP50 0.623 (mAP50-95 0.451), also essentially unchanged.
Training from scratch on 80 images fails completely: mAP50 0.0006 — no meaningful learning at all.
Key insight: with only 80 training images across 80 COCO classes, the pretrained weights carry almost all the signal; additional fine-tuning on this tiny set neither helps nor hurts (within noise).
The 80-image dataset is far too small for any real domain adaptation; a larger dataset (e.g., full COCO or a domain-specific set) is needed for fine-tuning to show a positive delta.
